full_judgment: 13. Then, the next question comes up for consideration as to whether the civil Court is the more appropriate forum for adjudication upon the petitioner's case given that before ordering for rectification in the company's Register of members, the impugned decision taken by the executive committee of the club is required to be declared illegal. It is true that jurisdiction of the civil Court is wider than this Court for dealing with a dispute of civil nature and unless any law specifically contains a provision barring the civil Court's jurisdiction, the civil Court is appropriate forum for seeking any declaration of civil nature. Because, in a Suit, while on the one hand, it is easy to resolve a complicated question of fact by taking oral evidence, on the other, provisions of Civil Procedure Code (CPC), Specific Relief Act, Evidence Act and other Civil laws can be applied without facing any limitation.
